ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a square ABCD, with A at the lower-left corner, B at the upper-left corner, C at the upper-right corner, and D at the lower-right corner. Point M is located at the midpoint of the upper side BC, and point N is located at the midpoint of the right side CD. From A, lines are drawn respectively to M and N, and θ is marked at the angle between rays AM and AN. Reasoning: According to the method, let the side length of the square be 2, and take A=(0,0), B=(0,2), C=(2,2), D=(2,0). Since M is the midpoint of BC, M=(1,2); since N is the midpoint of CD, N=(2,1). Thus vector AM=(1,2), AN=(2,1). The sine of the angle θ between the two vectors is |det(AM,AN)|/(|AM||AN|)=|1·1-2·2|/(sqrt(1^2+2^2)·sqrt(2^2+1^2))=3/(sqrt5·sqrt5)=3/5.

raw_record.question_text: $ABCD$ is a square, and $M$ and $N$ are the midpoints of $BC$ and $CD$ respectively. What is the value of $\sin\theta$?

method.method_draft: Use a coordinate/vector model. From the image, read that A is the bottom-left vertex of the square, B top-left, C top-right, D bottom-right, with segments AM and AN drawn and θ marked as the angle between AM and AN at A. From the text, use that M is the midpoint of BC and N is the midpoint of CD. Let the square have side length 2, so A=(0,0), B=(0,2), C=(2,2), D=(2,0). Then M=(1,2) and N=(2,1). The vectors are AM=(1,2) and AN=(2,1). Compute sinθ using the determinant formula for the angle between vectors: sinθ=|det(AM,AN)|/(|AM||AN|)=|1·1-2·2|/(sqrt(5)sqrt(5))=3/5.
